layout_dets.text: ABSTRACT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The critical pitting potential determined potentiostatically of pure Al in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 0.1N NaCl is —0.40V (SHE). This value is not greatly sensitive to tempera-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture (0-40°C), to small alloying additions of Mn or Mg, nor to thickness of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: oxide film produced by anodizing. The value is more active the higher the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Cl- concentration, but becomes more noble with additions to NaCl of nitrates,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chromates, acetates, benzoates, or sulfates. The latter act as pitting inhibitors

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which are effective in the order as listed. Dissolved Cu+ + in trace amounts

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deposit on the Al surface as Cu which then acts as an efficient cathode, shift-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing the corrosion potential of aluminum to the critical pitting potential. Trace

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: amounts of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and Pd++ act similarly. Anodized surfaces effectively

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: retard penetration of the oxide by Cu+ + thereby delaying onset of pitting,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: but they are not similarly effective when Al is coupled to Cu. The mechanism

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of pitting is interpreted in terms of competitive adsorption of Cl- with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: oxygen for sites on the metal surface. Extraneous anions compete in turn with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ions, making it necessary to shift the potential in the positive direction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in order for Cl- to adsorb followed by pit initiation. Similarities in adsorption

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parameters of various anions other thân Cl- on Al and 18-8 stainless steel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are pointed out.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Precise determination of the critical pitting poten-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tial of Al was first carried out by Kaesche (1) using

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: both potentiostatic and galvanostatic techniques. He

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: found that the potential above which, but not below,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Al undergoes pitting corrosion in 1M NaCl is —0.48V

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [std. H2 scale (SHE)] which value is independent of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pH between the interval pH 2-11. He also reported

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that the critical potential becomes more active (more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: negative) the higher the NaCl concentration between

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 0.1-4.0M NaCl. Bond et al. (2) measured the critical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting potential for zone-refined Al in 0.5M NaCl in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approximate agreement with the corresponding value

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reported by Kaesche.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Leckie and Uhlig (3) pointed out that the cathodic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: protection of aluminum, as usually practiced in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aerated saline media, consists of polarizing Al only

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: below the critical pitting potential and not below

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the open-circuit anode potential as is required for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steel. In principle, therefore, zinc is a possible sacri-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ficial anode for this purpose, but not iron. For stain-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: less steels, on the other hand, pitting corrosion can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: avoided in saline media such as sea water by coupling

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: either iron or zinc, since either metal succeeds in po-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: larizing the alloy below its critical pitting potential

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In view of the importance of the critical potential

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to the application of Al to saline environments, data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are reported herewith on the effect of temperature, of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: various anions and cations, of some alloying elements

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and of inhibiting salt concentrations on observed val-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ues. In addition, the mechanism of accelerated pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by traces of Cu+ + is discussed.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Experimental

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For most of the measurements, 99.99% Al electrodes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were employed measuring 1.5 cm long and 0.4 cm in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diameter. One end of each electrode was drilled and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tapped, allowing a threaded member attached to a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nickel wire to hold the electrode firmly against a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: glass tube separated by a water-tight Teflon gasket.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Only the electrode surface, totally immersed, Teflon,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and glass made contact with the electrolyte. Speci-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mens were polished to 3/0 emery paper followed by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pickling in 2N NaOH at 80°C for 5 min and then

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: washing in distilled water. A few measurements were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: also carried out on 99.4% Al and on alloys of 1.3%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mn-Al and 2.4% Mg-Al all of which were supplied by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: courtesy of the Aluminum Company of America.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The all-glass cell as previously described (3) was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: placed in an air thermostat maintained at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Temperatures could also be maintained at some value

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: above or below room temperature. At

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the glass

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cell was placed additionally in a water-ice bath. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: electrolyte was deaerated before measurements by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bubbling through it purified

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: previously passed over

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Cu turnings at 400°C.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The procedure was to polarize the electrode anodi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cally within the passive region for 5 min at —0.80V

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vs. saturated calomel electrode (SCE) or —0.56V

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (SHE) using a Wenking potentiostat in conjunction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with a chart recorder. This procedure achieved steady-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: state conditions before a step-by-step technique was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: applied by which the potential was increased 50 mV

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: every 5 min and the corresponding current noted. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: current remained relatively constant below the ap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proximate critical potential

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (<1 μA/cm²), but in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: creased sharply above by two or more orders of mag-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nitude. These measurements in turn were supple-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mented by longer time runs maintaining a given po-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tential near the critical value for at least 12 hr. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: least noble value at which pits could not be observed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: under a low-power microscope was taken as the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steady-state critical potential

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Reproducibility of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steady-state values was better than ±15 mV. All po-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tentials are reported with reference to the SHE.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As a check on some of the critical pitting potentials

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: obtained as described, immersion tests were also run

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: using pickled specimens of 99.4% Al measuring 1½ x

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ½ x 0.065 in. (3.8 x 1.3 x 0.17 cm). These were sus-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pended by means of a nylon thread through a hole

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: drilled in one end of the specimen and then placed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in closed 250 ml flasks for a period of 1-14 days. After

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the test period, the number of pits on the two main

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: faces of the specimen, visible under a low-power mi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: croscope, was counted.

layout_dets.text: CRITICAL PITTING POTENTIAL OF Al

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 1. Critical pitting potentials of 99.99% Al in 0.1M NaCl

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as a function of temperature.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steel is much more resistant to pitting corrosion at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: low temperatures compared to room temperature, but

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: susceptibility of aluminum is about the same. This

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: temperature effect refers only to initiation of pits and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not to rate of pit growth. Size of pits after a given

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: time depends on the cathodic reaction rate, the latter

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in turn usually proceeding more rapidly the higher

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the temperature.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Effect of anion concentration and alloying.—It is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: known that pitting of Al is pronounced in presence of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chloride ions. In sulfates, on the other hand, Al elec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trodes can be polarized anodically without exhibiting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a critical pitting potential or showing any evidence of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting attack. In perchlorate solutions, however, pit-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ting occurs, as well as in bromide and iodide solutions,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: although the pitting tendency is less pronounced than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in chloride solutions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The respective steady-state critical potentials in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: each environment are listed in Table I including the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: value in 0.5M NaCl reported by Bond et al. (2) and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the nonsteady-state values reported earlier by Kaes-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: che (1). The more active the critical potential, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: greater is the tendency for pitting to occur. The effect

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of temperature is small in either 0.1M NaCl or NaBr.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Alloys of Al containing a small amount of Mg or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mn tend to pit more than does pure Al, although the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shift of potential is small. For 99.4% Al, the critical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potential is the same as for 99.99% Al within experi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mental error of the measurements. Porter and Hadden

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (4) reported that immersion tests in various supply

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: waters showed that superpure Al tended to pit some-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: what less than did Ai alloys, although the final pit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: depth was almost the same.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ting shift the critical potential of Al in halide solu-

layout_dets.text: tions in the noble direction corresponding to improved

layout_dets.text: corrosion resistance. This was shown previously to be

layout_dets.text: true for stainless steels (3, 5). If extraneous salts are
